checks.id: time: each moment shows the clock's frame, clamped to the window
time: a phone that opens at 9 s shows 9 s at once, and the ship is already there
time: two phones on the same clock draw the same picture
time: it follows the trusted clock, frame by frame
time: at the end it holds the last picture, the still, and asks for no more frames
time: the film's last picture is the poster's pose
time: a new window is a new film, from its own start
time: a 2 s window enters for 1 s and settles for 1 s
still: "moved" shows the still, the poster's pose, with its caption and name
still: with no trusted clock, or no window, the still, the same on every phone
reduced: the game's Reduce motion shows the still, marked data-motion="reduced", and asks for no frames
reduced: the still comes in with one 80 ms fade, and nothing else moves
reduced: turned off mid-window, it seeks to the clock
lifecycle: suspended, it stands still and asks for no frames
lifecycle: resumed, it seeks to the clock, replaying nothing
lifecycle: reconnecting (stale), it stands still where it was
lifecycle: live again, it seeks to the clock
lifecycle: concealed, nothing of the film is drawn or named, and no frames run
lifecycle: shown again, it seeks to the clock
lifecycle: one frame loop at most, whatever the updates
lifecycle: dispose() twice is safe; after it nothing runs and frame() is null
caption: 24 px above the bottom safe area the shell gives, and it follows a change
privacy: every input the film does not know is refused, a course's above all
privacy: nothing the film draws or says names a course, a side or an office
